name: agents-inc-monorepo
//: Prettier is declared once, here. Prettier walks up from each file to the nearest config, so this covers every workspace including packages/*-config. It is also why packages/cli keeps its own formatting for free: packages/cli/prettier.config.mjs sits nearer to the CLI's files than this field does, so it wins for everything under packages/cli and this config never touches them. Prettier does NOT walk up for .prettierignore, which is why `format` runs from the root rather than fanning out through turbo — see the scripts below.

scripts.//prepare: Moved here from packages/cli when the CLI stopped being the repository root. Git hooks live in .husky/ at the root of the repository, so the package that installs them has to be the root package.
scripts.//format: One run from the root, deliberately not `turbo format`. Prettier reads .prettierignore only from its working directory, so fanning out per workspace made the root ignore invisible and reformatted the vendored catalog it exists to protect — which then reads as drift against the generator. The glob stays as it was: widening it to md/json is a separate decision, not part of fixing this.
scripts.//deps:check: Four checks, all of which only make sense across workspaces and none of which any workspace's own gates can see. syncpack compares dependency ranges; the second compares each workspace's tsconfig.json to the shared configs it is meant to extend; the third does the same for vitest.config.*, added 2026-08-07; the fourth does the same for eslint.config.*, added 2026-08-08. packages/cli/tsconfig.json extended nothing for months while tsc, eslint, both suites, tsup and turbo typecheck all stayed green, because every one of them reads whatever the config says — and a Vitest config is read exactly the same way, so a suite that has stopped agreeing with its siblings about globals, includes or clearMocks is green in its own workspace and invisible from every other one. The ESLint case is the same defect with a quieter symptom: packages/cli composed the shared rule set by hand instead of extending it, so the shared base's additions beyond typescript-eslint's recommended set never reached it, and `eslint .` stayed clean the whole time because a rule that is not enabled reports nothing. How a workspace stands apart on purpose — the //no-shared-* key, why the value is a reason rather than true, and which of the three axes a missing config exits rather than fails — is one convention across all three, written once at packages/cli/.ai-docs/reference/monorepo-layout.md -> 'A workspace that stands apart records it in its own package.json' and detailed per axis in the three subsections under it. Do not restate it here; it drifted the last time it was in two places. The scripts live in packages/cli because that is the only workspace with a test runner and a scripts/ convention to keep them honest — the same reason the vendored-catalog check lives there and guards the web side. Each takes its root from its own location, so the paths here are invocations and not working directories.
scripts.//deps:dead: knip across every workspace: files nothing imports, exports nothing reads, dependencies nothing uses, and imports no manifest declares. Deliberately NOT part of deps:check and deliberately not a gate anywhere — owner's ruling, and the shape of the output is the reason. deps:check answers a yes/no question in 0.2s and belongs in a hook; this one produces a few hundred lines whose value is entirely in reading them, and roughly all of the first run's were the same finding wearing different names — a barrel re-exporting a symbol every caller imports from the source module instead. That is a judgement about how the barrels should read, not a defect to fail a commit over. Run it from time to time by hand, read the output, and open the deletions it justifies. It exits non-zero whenever it finds anything, so wiring it into a gate would break every commit from the first one. What the tuning in knip.jsonc buys is stated per workspace there; the short version is that a finding you can refute by reading is a gap in that config rather than a finding, and the first pass was iterated until the survivors held up. Where it cannot help: knip reports files, exports and dependencies, not the members of an object type or an unread function parameter — the two finds CLI-461 left behind are both of that shape, and grep is what settles them. Baseline and verdicts: todo/plans/CLI-464-dead-code-baseline-2026-08-09.md.

//lint-staged: ESLint then Prettier, on the files a commit stages. ESLint sat here once, left when packages/cli stopped being the repository root, and came back on 2026-08-08. The reason it left was mechanical: ESLint 9 resolved a flat config from the working directory and its ancestors, lint-staged runs its commands from the git root, and this repository has no eslint.config at its root — so after the merge the entry failed on every commit staging a .ts file. ESLint 10 resolves the config from the directory of the FILE being linted, and that is the whole of what changed. Measured from the root: `eslint packages/cli/src/cli/base-command.ts` exits 0 having loaded packages/cli/eslint.config.js, projectService carve-out and all, where under 9 it exited 2 with "couldn't find an eslint.config file". The type-aware rules really do run in that per-file invocation, and that file is the proof rather than a sample — it carries an eslint-disable for no-unnecessary-condition and reportUnusedDisableDirectives is an error in that package, so a run where the rule had not fired would have failed on the now-pointless directive. The other half of the old argument died separately: every workspace declares eslint ^10 and one hoisted copy serves them all, so there is no binary split to appeal to either. There is still no root fallback — `eslint vitest.config.mjs` at the root exits 2, because nothing above it holds a config. What did NOT move is `lint` on the turbo line in .husky/pre-commit, and the rule inventory is the reason. Some of the rules every workspace enables are type-aware — typescript-eslint's recommendedTypeChecked, plus no-unnecessary-condition from the shared base — and a type-aware verdict reads a whole TypeScript program, so a staged change can raise a report in a file the commit does not touch and no staged-file run can see it. Nothing else in the seven configs needs more than the file it is given: the config-gate import bans are no-restricted-imports, which matches the literal specifier string through `ignore` and never resolves a module, the dynamic-import and task-ID bans are no-restricted-syntax AST selectors, and there is no import-cycle plugin anywhere in the repository. So this entry is the fast half rather than a replacement — a violation in a file you staged fails here in ~4s instead of ~19s further down the hook, and the fixable ones are fixed and re-staged before turbo sees them at all. `--fix` rather than a check, for the same reason prettier here is `--write`. Three patterns rather than one, and both parts of that are deliberate. lint-staged runs different patterns concurrently, so two of them writing the same file is a race — these three are disjoint by construction and together match exactly the 1596 files the single `*.{ts,tsx,js,json,yaml,yml,md}` pattern matched before. packages/vitest-config is named because it holds the one tracked .ts file in the repository with no eslint.config above it, and that is by design rather than an omission: it ships node.js as plain JavaScript with node.d.ts hand-written beside it, so there is nothing there to lint. A single config-less file poisons the whole invocation — `eslint <any linted file> packages/vitest-config/node.d.ts` exits 2 for both, not just for the one — so its declaration file gets formatting only. Add a workspace of that shape and it belongs in both of the first two patterns. `--no-warn-ignored` is the same story seen from the other side: a staged file inside a globalIgnores (generated types, vendored copies) or matched by no `files` block is one warning per file otherwise, and a hook that prints noise on ordinary commits stops being read. Prettier stays here for the inverse reason to ESLint's — it does NOT want per-workspace working directories, see the note on `format` above.
